AbstractText.Label: STUDY QUESTION
AbstractText.content: What is the prevalence and functional consequence of ANOS1 (KAL1) mutations in a group of men with congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (CHH)?

AbstractText.Label: SUMMARY ANSWER
AbstractText.content: Three of forty-two (7.1%) patients presented ANOS1 mutations, including a novel splice site mutation leading to exon skipping and a novel contiguous gene deletion associated with ichthyosis.

AbstractText.Label: WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY
AbstractText.content: CHH is characterized by lack of pubertal development and infertility, due to deficient production, secretion or action of GnRH, and can be associated with anosmia/hyposmia (Kallmann syndrome, KS) or with a normal sense of smell (normosmic CHH). Mutations in the anosmin-1 (ANOS1) gene are responsible for the X-linked recessive form of KS.

AbstractText.Label: STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION
AbstractText.content: This cross-sectional study included 42 unrelated men with CHH (20 with KS and 22 with normosmic CHH).

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS
AbstractText.content: Patients were screened for mutations in the ANOS1 gene by DNA sequencing. Identified mutations were further investigated by RT-PCR analysis and multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) analysis.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE
AbstractText.content: Hemizygous mutations were identified in three (7.1%) KS cases: a novel splice acceptor site mutation (c.542-1G>C), leading to skipping of exon 5 in the ANOS1 transcript in a patient with self-reported normosmia (but hyposmic upon testing); a recurrent nonsense mutation (c.571C>T, p.Arg191*); and a novel 4.8 Mb deletion involving ANOS1 and eight other genes (VCX3B, VCX2, PNPLA4, VCX, STS, HDHD1, VCX3A and NLGN4X) in KS associated with ichthyosis.

AbstractText.Label: LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION
AbstractText.content: Objective olfactory testing was not performed in all cases of self-reported normosmia and this may have underestimated the olfactory deficits.

AbstractText.Label: WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS
AbstractText.content: This study further expands the spectrum of known genetic defects associated with CHH and suggests that patients with self-reported normal olfactory function should not be excluded from ANOS1 genetic testing.

AbstractText.Label: STUDY FUNDING/COMPETING INTEREST(S)
AbstractText.content: This study was funded by the Portuguese Foundation for Science and Technology. The authors have no conflicts of interest.
